items.example: It might be a photo of a street market in a big city.
Maybe they are waiting for a delayed train.

note.en: Goes at the start of the clause; 'perhaps' is slightly more neutral.
note.es: Va al principio de la oración; «perhaps» es algo más neutro.

items.example: I guess the woman is a teacher, because she is standing in front of a class.
It's possible that the two men are colleagues.

note.en: Useful in Speaking part 2 to describe a photo you are unsure about.
note.es: Útil en Speaking 2 para describir una foto de la que no estás seguro.

items.example: They must be on holiday, because they are carrying large suitcases.

note.en: Use 'must' only when the evidence is strong.
note.es: Usa «must» solo si las pruebas son sólidas.

items.example: There's a good chance that the shop will be closed on Monday.
I wouldn't be surprised if the match was moved indoors.

note.en: Followed by a past tense, even when talking about the future.
note.es: Va con pasado aunque hables del futuro.

items.example: It could well be that the building is a library rather than a school.
It is conceivable that fewer people will own cars within twenty years.

items.phrase: One can only speculate as to whether …
items.example: One can only speculate as to whether the delay was caused by staff shortages.
Chances are the cafe will be full by the time we get there.
It is highly likely that demand for remote learning will continue to grow.
